results.title: Standard Chartered Moves $2 Trillion Stablecoin Call to 2030
highlights:
Highlights
Standard Chartered now expects the stablecoin market to reach$2 trillion by 2030,two years later than its earlier timeline of 2028.
Total stablecoin supply has moved within a$300 billion to$320 billion band for a year and now sits near$309 billion.
Usage keeps rising,with monthly transfer value averaging just under$10 trillion in 2026,up from$4 trillion in 2025.
Standard Chartered has not given up on its$2 trillion call for stablecoins.It has simply moved the finishing line.In a report released on 14 October 2026,the bank said it now expects the market to reach that size by 2030 rather than 2028,after supply growth across the Crypto sector stalled this year.
Geoffrey Kendrick,the bank's global head of digital assets research,sees the pause as part of a cycle,not a permanent shift.In his view,it reflects a quiet period for crypto markets rather than a lasting change in demand.
The more interesting part of the report may be what is happening beneath the headline number.Supply has flattened,yet stablecoins are moving between wallets far more often than they did a year ago.
Why Has the Timeline Slipped by Two Years?The simple answer is that the supply of stablecoins has stopped climbing.Over the past 12 months it has barely left a band of$300 billion to$320 billion,and Kendrick put the current figure at roughly$309 billion.
He pointed out that this has happened before.In earlier spells when supply went sideways or shrank,it picked up again as soon as crypto prices found their footing,which is why the bank has kept its$2 trillion estimate intact and only pushed back the date.

highlights:
What stablecoin card adoption numbers actually measure
  
A stablecoin card can work at millions of shops without those shops ever receiving stablecoins.It can also reach that scale before many customers have used it.The acceptance network already exists;the new card connects to it.Actual use leaves different evidence:completed purchases,repeat customers,and spending over a stated period.A launch announcement may establish where a card could work while leaving unanswered how often people use it and what currency merchants receive.
In its April 30,2025 announcement,Visa said cards issued through its arrangement with Bridge could be used at more than 150 million merchant locations accepting Visa.That figure described the existing network’s reach at the time.The release announced a way to spend stablecoin balances through that network,rather than retailers introducing cryptocurrency checkouts.It gave no completed-purchase total for the new card product and no count of regular users.The merchant number could therefore remain unchanged,even as use of those cards grew.
At the checkout
A grocery purchase can begin with a stablecoin balance while the supermarket processes an ordinary card sale.The customer selects the card,and the store charges for the groceries.The stablecoins can be converted into ordinary currency,so the merchant receives local currency,according to AlphaWire.The store can complete the sale without asking the customer to send tokens to a wallet.In this arrangement,stablecoins fund the purchase on the customer’s side;the retailer does not need to retain them.

US accounting proposal could clear path for corporate stablecoin adoption
A proposed change to US accounting standards could make it easier for corporations to hold and use stablecoins without compromising their reported cash positions,according to a new report from Stripe-backed blockchain Tempo.
The Financial Accounting Standards Board(FASB)is considering allowing qualifying stablecoins to be classified as cash equivalents on corporate balance sheets.Currently,companies may have to report stablecoin holdings as other assets,which can affect liquidity ratios and compliance with loan covenants.
Tempo said the proposed treatment would depend on whether companies have direct redemption rights with stablecoin issuers.This means two companies holding identical USDC tokens could receive different accounting treatment depending on their arrangements with Circle.
For example,Coinbase classified USDC and other payment stablecoins as cash equivalents in its 2025 annual report,supported by its direct redemption arrangement with Circle.
The proposal follows the passage of the GENIUS Act,which established federal requirements for payment stablecoin issuers.FASB’s separate initiative addresses how businesses account for those assets.
The accounting proposal remains open for public comment until Nov.19.
Global watchdog flags stablecoin risks,AI threats ahead of G20
The FSB,a global financial watchdog,has outlined financial stability risks associated with artificial intelligence and regulatory concerns surrounding stablecoins.
In a letter published Monday,FSB Chair Andrew Bailey warned that cross-border mechanisms for stablecoin oversight and crisis management“remain immature or are not yet developed.”In its 2025 review,the FSB found that 11 of 28 surveyed jurisdictions had finalized stablecoin regulatory frameworks.

results.title: Stablecoins and tokenised assets explained: What Indian investors should know - CNBC TV18
highlights:
What are stablecoins and how are they used?Stablecoins are digital tokens designed to maintain a relatively stable value against an asset,usually a currency such as the US dollar.They can facilitate transfers between digital-asset platforms and are also being explored for cross-border payments,remittances and business settlements.
A global management consulting firm McKinsey,in an analysis with blockchain analytics firm Artemis Analytics,estimated that stablecoin payment activity reached around$390 billion in 2025,more than double the previous year's level.
However,this remains small compared with conventional payment networks,and blockchain transaction volumes should not automatically be equated with payments for goods and services.
Vikaas M Sachdeva,CEO of BitDelta India,an independent,India-focused virtual digital asset(VDA)and cryptocurrency trading platform,said blockchain could reduce intermediaries and speed up settlement in certain cross-border transactions.However,he noted that India's existing payment systems,including UPI,IMPS and RTGS,already work efficiently,making it important to assess where the technology offers a genuine advantage.
A stablecoin is not the same as money held in a bank account.
Its ability to maintain its value depends on factors such as the assets backing it,the issuer's financial position and redemption arrangements.Risks include inadequate reserves,issuer failure,loss of the intended price peg,cyberattacks and restrictions on withdrawals.
Sachdeva advised investors to examine the issuer,reserve disclosures,custody arrangements and redemption rights rather than relying on the label 'stablecoin'.
For Indian users,a dollar-linked stablecoin is not the Indian rupee and should not be assumed to be an RBI-authorised payment instrument.
